name: Should I use a tub-shower combo or a walk-in shower in a guest bathroom?

mainEntity.name: For a guest bathroom, is a tub-shower combo better than a walk-in shower for resale and daily use?
mainEntity.text: For a guest bathroom, is a tub-shower combo better than a walk-in shower for resale and daily use?

acceptedAnswer.text: The right choice depends on function and market expectations. A tub-shower combo offers flexibility because it supports bathing children, serving different guest needs, and appealing to buyers who still want at least one tub in the home. A walk-in shower can make a small guest bathroom feel larger and is often preferred for a cleaner, more modern look. In Los Angeles-area homes, the decision often comes down to whether the guest bath is the only secondary bathroom or one of several. If it is the only tub in the house, keeping a tub may broaden resale appeal. If the home already has another tub and the guest bath is tight, a well-designed shower can improve everyday use. The best choice is the one that fits the room size, supports the intended users, and does not create a cramped or awkward layout.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tub-shower combo is often more flexible for resale, while a walk-in shower can feel more spacious and modern. The better choice depends on how the bathroom is used, who the guests are, and whether preserving a tub matters for future buyers.
